I took a short trip to Myanmar two months back, thought I would share my photos with you guys!
Beautiful pictures! I want to travel there some day, any thoughts on your visit?

Thanks! It's a great place! Personally didn't think much of Yangon (the main city), except for the Circle Line train ride. The people in Yangon aren't as warm and welcoming as those in the villages and smaller towns outside of Yangon - Stay a day or two max, and take a bus out towards Inle Lake and Bagan!

Some recommend taking the train, but it's only for the masochistic travellers. The busses are extremely comfortable and reclines far enough to sleep.

Weather-wise, it's brutally hot and dry in the hot season, no joke. I found this to be a good guide.

I started my last Morrowind play through using OpenMW and apart from a few bugs it worked really well. It's awesome seeing the Morrowind community be able to recreate the entire engine. What are your experiences using OpenMW so far? Or if you did not try it yet: What's keeping you?

I've been using OpenMW since version 0.31.0 and have been enjoying it quite a bit. This is actually the first time playing Morrowind for me, so being able to enjoy it is just great. Aside from some of the bug, there is nothing that breaks the game for it.

Currently, I'm trying to get the name Telvanni Hortator to finish the three Hortator houses and I've done three of the four Nerevarine's. Also took out the Assassins in Mournhold. I've got so much money, I'm gonna go enchant some stuff.

Interesting choice to start your first play through using OpenMW. What made you decide to use OpenMW instead of the regular Morrowind (with enhanced graphics mods)?

Also, maybe a stupid question seeing how far along the main quest you are, but how are you enjoying Morrowind?

I'm on Linux. I don't rely on WINE for anything.

I freakin love Morrowind! I played Skyrim on my PS3 and loved it so I started following the development of OpenMW since version 0.19 or something that long ago. Heck, I remember when rendering water was a huge deal. I also played a little bit of Daggerfall, but like WINE, there's just too many problems with DOSBOX for me to really get full enjoyment out of it.

Ah of course, OpenMW must be a godsend for Linux users.

OpenMW has been in development a long time, I remember way back there were several Morrowind reimplementation projects going. Still amazing considering how far the OpenMW team has gotten. Really really great work.

A godsend is putting it very lightly. ;)

Since Skyrim and playing a little bit of Daggerfall I fell in love with the lore. Being able to play all of Morrowind on Linux is just amazing.

I have half a mind of installing Ubuntu on my computer (currently use it at work and really like it) just to see how it stacks up with Windows when looking at games. I doubt it can replace Windows currently but would be really interesting to experience the state of Linux gaming for myself.

It's not for everyone. For me, I have been using Linux exclusively since 2006. So, for me, I usually just played console games and only the very few computer games (mostly UT2K4). But, lately, because of HIB and Valve, we have over 1000 games (I have something like 370 games on Steam for Linux). But, not many AAA games. This is supposed to be changing pretty soon because of the Steam Boxes being released in November. But, the AAA games we do have are fantastic. And if you like indie games, there are plenty of them.

But, Linux isn't for everyone. Don't put too much faith into it in case it doesn't work for you, you won't have lost much time.
